title: Progressive Web Apps Quick Guide
description: Find a short explanation and a worked example for each idea in the Progressive Web Apps course.

entries.name: Start with a useful website
entries.summary: A progressive web app starts as a working website.

example.code:
Reading list

Choose a book for today.

entries.name: Describe the app in a manifest
entries.summary: A manifest is a JSON file that describes the app name, start address and display choices.

entries.name: Link the manifest and icons
entries.summary: The page must link its manifest. Icons should be real image files in the sizes declared by the manifest.

example.code:
<link rel="manifest" href="/manifest.webmanifest">
<meta name="theme-color" content="#174a8b">
<!-- In the manifest, add real 192x192 and 512x512 PNG icons with their actual sizes. -->

entries.name: Register a service worker
entries.summary: A service worker is a script that the browser can run separately from the page.

entries.name: Install an offline page
entries.summary: The install event is a chance to prepare files for later use.

entries.name: Give navigation an offline fallback
entries.summary: A fetch handler can try the network first and use a saved page when that request fails.

entries.name: Choose a cache rule for a purpose
entries.summary: Cache-first uses a stored response before trying the network.

entries.name: Remove your own old caches
entries.summary: The activate event can tidy old cache versions.

entries.name: Understand a waiting update
entries.summary: A new worker may wait while the old one still controls open pages.

entries.name: Save a small local preference
entries.summary: A page can remember a small choice in localStorage.

entries.name: Treat network hints as hints
entries.summary: The online and offline events are useful clues.

example.code:
window.addEventListener("offline", () => console.log("The browser reports offline."));
window.addEventListener("online", () => console.log("The browser reports online. Try the request again."));

entries.name: Test and reset your practice app
entries.summary: A PWA needs tests for first visit, repeat visit, offline use and updates.

example.code:
Open Application tools on your own local project.
Check manifest errors and worker scope.
Load once online, then test offline navigation.
Change sw.js and inspect the waiting version.
For a clean test, unregister only your practice worker and clear only its app caches.
